articles.author: Sommer Brugal
articles.summary: Some Democrats see Angie Nixon's Senate loss in Florida as a warning about running too far left. But her results with Hispanic voters challenge that idea, an Axios analysis found. Hispanic-majority precincts that some feared would reject her politics swung more than 21 points toward Democrats from 2024 and gave her a slight edge over moderate gubernatorial candidate David Jolly. Why it matters: Democrats gained more ground in Florida than in most states this year despite falling short in the two biggest races. Whether they can finish climbing out of their hole will shape the party's 2028 chances in a state seen as a Republican stronghold. " There definitely was a broad blue shift, it just wasn't deep enough," Daniel Smith, a University of Florida political science professor, tells Axios. "But you don't get to these close numbers without non-party affiliates and Republicans voting Democrat." The big picture: Florida swung further toward Democrats than Georgia's gubernatorial race or Ohio's Senate race, yet Florida Democrats had a bigger hole to climb out of.
